title: The Private Production of Safety Outside Options and the Burden of Protection
abstract: arXiv:2611.30735v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Protective interventions are typically evaluated by their ability to prevent harm. Yet protection also raises a distinct question: who bears the burden of adjusting to violence? I examine this allocation of protective adjustment using four randomized interventions in the United States. An offer of permanent housing assistance increases separation from a baseline partner combined with stable independent housing by 12.52 percentage points. Assignment to active police-response protocols reduces observed victim-only departures and increases suspect-only departures. Assignment to an emergency protection order increases documented directions for suspects to leave. These findings reveal two margins of the same allocation problem: housing assistance expands victims' ability to establish an independent residence, while enforcement shifts displacement obligations toward suspects. Protective policies thus shape not only the opportunities for safety

translated_title: 安全外部选项的私人供给与保护的负担
translated_abstract: 保护性干预措施通常以其防止伤害的能力来评估。然而，保护还引发了一个截然不同的问题：谁承担了适应暴力的负担？本文利用美国的四项随机干预实验研究了这种保护性调整责任的分配问题。提供永久性住房援助使受害者与基线伴侣分离并拥有稳定独立住房的比例提高了12.52个百分点。被分配到主动警务响应协议减少了仅观察到受害者离开的情况，同时增加了仅嫌疑人离开的情况。被分配紧急保护令增加了记录在案的嫌疑人离开的指示。这些发现揭示了同一分配问题的两个边际：住房援助扩大了受害者建立独立住所的能力，而执法措施则将搬迁义务转移给嫌疑人。因此，保护性政策不仅塑造了获得安全的机会……
tldr: 该论文通过美国四项随机干预实验发现，保护性政策会重新分配适应暴力的调整负担——住房援助扩大受害者建立独立住所的能力，而执法措施则将搬迁义务从受害者转移给施暴嫌疑人。
en_tdlr: Using four randomized interventions in the United States, this paper shows that protective policies reallocate the burden of adjusting to violence: housing assistance expands victims' capacity to establish independent residences, while enforcement shifts displacement obligations toward suspects.
